findings.evidence: Lines 215-216 and 223-224 are character-identical apart from the final `eq_div_iff (by positivity)` / `le_div_iff₀ (by positivity)`; line 247 repeats `norm_I, norm_mul, Complex.norm_two, norm_real, Real.norm_of_nonneg hρ.le`.
findings.fix: Add `theorem norm_elasticSMatrix {ρ : ℝ} (hρ : 0 < ρ) (t : ℂ) : ‖elasticSMatrix ρ t‖ = 2 * ρ * ‖t - I / (2 * ρ)‖` (one chain, once), then prove the circle and disc versions by `rw [norm_elasticSMatrix hρ, eq_div_iff …]`/`le_div_iff₀` and derive `hc` from it (or from `norm_div` alone).
findings.issue: `norm_elasticSMatrix_eq_one_iff_norm_sub_eq` (215-216) and `norm_elasticSMatrix_le_one_iff_norm_sub_le` (223-224) repeat the identical eight-step chain `elasticSMatrix_eq_mul_sub, norm_mul, norm_mul, norm_mul, norm_I, Complex.norm_two, norm_real, Real.norm_of_nonneg`, differing only in `eq_div_iff` vs `le_div_iff₀`; `hc` at 246-247 computes the same `‖2 * ρ‖` fact a third time. The reusable fact `‖elasticSMatrix ρ t‖ = 2 * ρ * ‖t - I / (2 * ρ)‖` is never stated, so a rename of any of those norm lemmas breaks three proofs.

findings.evidence: Lines 36-40: the `rw` chain ends in `← one_apply_eq (α := 𝕜) (default : n)`, after which the goal is an iff between two matrix-entry equations closed by `refine ⟨fun h ↦ by rw [h], …⟩`.
findings.fix: Prove the two directions forwards from `hS`: forward, `congr_fun₂ h default default` rewritten by `hS` and `one_apply_eq` then `exact_mod_cast`; backward, `ext i j` and close with `hS` plus the hypothesis. Keep only `← pow_eq_one_iff_of_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) two_ne_zero` as a statement-level rewrite.
findings.issue: The proof does not prove the equivalence; it rewrites the goal's right side `‖S₀₀‖ = 1` backwards through `← pow_eq_one_iff_of_nonneg`, `← RCLike.ofReal_inj (K := 𝕜)`, `← hS default default` and `← one_apply_eq (α := 𝕜) (default : n)` until it becomes `(star S * S) default default = (1 : Matrix n n 𝕜) default default`. The direction and the explicit `(α := 𝕜)`/`(default : n)` ascriptions exist only to steer `rw` away from the `1 : Matrix n n 𝕜` on the other side of the iff, which obscures why the step is sound and breaks if `one_apply_eq`'s form changes.

summary: Proofs are mostly readable and robust, but one reusable fact (the modulus of the single-channel S-matrix) is hidden inside two duplicated eight-lemma rewrite chains, and the new one-by-one unitary lemma proves itself by rewriting its statement backwards into a matrix-entry equation.
